# opstracer_service_data_sources (Resource)

Which observability connection a service reads from, per provider. Providers not listed keep the org default connection. Destroying the resource puts every listed provider back to the default.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opstracer_service_data_sources" "checkout" {
  service_id = opstracer_service.checkout.id
  sources = {
    grafana = { choice = "connection", connection_id = opstracer_observability_connection.grafana.id }
    sentry  = { choice = "off" }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `service_id` (String) ID of the service.
- `sources` (Attributes Map) Choices keyed by provider type (`datadog`, `grafana`, `sentry`, `newrelic`, `cloudwatch`, `gcp`, `railway`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--sources))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `service_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--sources"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sources`

Optional:

- `choice` (String) Required. `default` (the org default connection), `connection` (the one in `connection_id`) or `off` (do not read this provider).
- `connection_id` (String) Observability connection to read from. Required when `choice` is `connection`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import opstracer_service_data_sources.checkout <service-id>
```
